title: GPU pool early warning signal research & handoff
body:
Summary:

This is a research + handoff doc for an early-warning detection layer for Dedicated GPU pools. Goal: detect subtle, slow-onset pool degradations (minutes-to-hours) before customer-facing latency/throughput SLOs are violated. Current alerts detect large spikes but miss creeping degradation where tail latency climbs and throughput oscillates due to cross-tenant interference and scheduling inefficiencies.

Why this matters:
- Customers on Dedicated expect predictable throughput; creeping degradations are the most embarrassing incidents because they erode confidence but are noisy to reproduce.
- Runbook responses are reactive (evict, scale), but we often discover the problem only after token-level cost/regression alerts fire. An earlier signal gives time to investigate and apply safe mitigations.

High-level approach:
1) Define composite signals that correlate with upcoming SLO violation: small-step latency drift, kernel retry counts, allocator backoff events, KV-cache miss amplification, and queue depth skew across instances.
2) Prototype PromQL and SQL (clickhouse) queries to compute short-window derivatives and anomaly scores.
3) Run experiments during low-risk windows (canary regions / night windows) and collect labeled examples for 4–6 weeks.
4) Hand off rules and a lightweight playbook for on-call to act on early alerts.

Quick timeline (what happened so far):
- 2025-01-10: Initial idea after noisy weekend where region eu-west had a 15% sustained throughput drop for 3 hours; standard autoscaler never triggered because CPU/GPU utilization stayed within thresholds.
- 2025-01-17: Marco ran exploratory queries, found KV-cache miss rate had a 2x uptick ~18 minutes before throughput dip.
- 2025-01-25: Evelyn implemented a prototype Prometheus recording rule and a quick dashboard.
- 2025-02-05: Small simulation (synthetic tenant hammer) validated that kernel retry spikes and allocator backpressure precede latency creep in ~70% of runs.
- 2025-02-12: This doc created as handoff for broader SRE review and bake-in into runbook.

Candidate signals (novel / combined):
- KV cache miss amplification: fraction of requests with miss_count > X in 1m window (prefers prefix-sensitive workloads).
- Kernel retry rate: GPU driver/kernel-level retry counters per instance per minute (normalized by requests).
- Small-slot queue skew: variance of queue depth across worker slots (high skew indicates tenant localized contention).
- Micro-latency drift: 95th-99th derivative over 5–10m windows for short prompts (seq_len < 64).
- Allocator backoff events: short bursts of allocation failures/retries logged by allocator (counts per minute).
- CPU jitter on host: standard deviation of host CPU steal/softirq across 1m buckets (indicates noisy hypervisor activity).

PromQL examples (prototype):
- KV cache miss rate (per-pool):
  sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west"}[2m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west"}[2m]))

- Kernel retry surge (normalized):
  sum(rate(gpu_kernel_retries_total{env="dedicated"}[1m])) by (instance) / (sum(rate(inference_requests_total{pool="dedicated-eu-west"}[1m])) by (instance) + 1e-6)

- Micro-latency drift (5m derivative):
  deriv(quantile_over_time(0.95, request_duration_seconds{pool="dedicated-eu-west", seq_len="short"}[10m])[5m:]) > 0.02

ClickHouse / SQL style check (for longer history):
- Find 30–90 minute windows where 95p latency increases > 30% and preceding 20 minutes show >= 1.5x kernel_retry_rate:
  SELECT pool, window_start, pct95_latency, kernel_retry_rate_before FROM experiments WHERE pct95_latency > base_pct95 * 1.3 AND kernel_retry_rate_before > base_kernel_retry * 1.5

Alerting heuristic (draft):
- Phase 1 (informational): Composite anomaly score > threshold for 10 minutes => create SRE/infrastructure dir chart entry (no pager) and post to #sre-ops.
- Phase 2 (page to oncall): Composite score persists for 20+ minutes OR micro-latency drift crosses hard threshold (95p > 2x baseline) => page on-call with short context and link to runbook section.

On-call quick actions (draft steps):
- Step 0: Confirm: open dashboard (dashboards/redwood/gpu-pool-health) and look at: 95/99 latency, throughput, KV miss rate, kernel retries, allocator backoffs.
- Step 1: Identify scope: is issue pool-wide or subset of instances? Use instance heatmap -> if skewed to < 30% of instances, suspect local contention.
- Step 2: Soft mitigations (non-disruptive): drain new small batch traffic to suspect instances (adjust routing weight by -50% for 5m), toggle per-tenant soft-quotas if available.
- Step 3: If soft mitigations fail and composite score keeps rising: provision temporary burst capacity (if Dedicated plan allows) or trigger rapid scale-out (if autoscaler policy supports scale-factor for degraded-signal).
- Step 4: If throughput still degrading or kernel retries spike further: schedule targeted eviction of top noisy tenant(s) from suspect instances (follow eviction checklist).
- Step 5: Post-incident: collect traces and kernel logs, annotate ticket SRE-4382, attach candidate root-cause signals and timeline.

Commands & useful queries for on-call (cheat-sheet):
- kubectl get pods -n inference -l pool=dedicated-eu-west -o wide
- curl "http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=<PROMQL>" | jq .data.result
- alloc-ctl list-backoffs --pool dedicated-eu-west --since 30m
- gpu-metrics dump --instance $INSTANCE --since 20m > /tmp/gpu-dump.log

Experimental threshold suggestions (tunable):
- Composite anomaly score (weighted): KV_miss_weight=0.25, kernel_retry_weight=0.3, micro_latency_weight=0.25, allocator_backoff_weight=0.15, cpu_jitter_weight=0.05. Phase 1 score > 0.4, Phase 2 score > 0.7.
- Micro-latency drift soft threshold: 95p derivative > 0.015 (15ms on a 1s baseline) sustained 10m.

Simulation plan (how to validate):
- Week 1: Run synthetic tenant patterns on canary pool to create labeled positive cases. Capture metrics at 10s resolution.
- Week 2–4: Turn on informational signals in eu-west during night windows, review false positives, tune weights.
- Week 5–6: If FP rate < 15% and TP coverage > 65% for historical incidents, escalate to Phase 2 alerting with on-call paging for a single region.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Too many false positives -> alert fatigue. Mitigation: start informational only and iterate.
- Actions like eviction are disruptive; prefer scaled mitigation (routing weight) as first step.
- Some metrics (kernel retries) rely on driver-level counters that may not be present on older hardware; fallback to micro-latency-only signal for those pools.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: What is a good baseline window for each pool? 7d? 14d? (affects baselining for derivative/percentile).
- Q2: Do we have the telemetry for kernel retries uniformly across Dedicated racks? (Marco to audit by 2025-03-08).
- Q3: Can console routing accept transient weight adjustments via API (SRE runbooks prefer automated weight toggles)? (Evelyn to prototype API by 2025-02-28).
- TODO: Add a small lightweight runbook fragment for on-call pager message templates.

Handoff / next owners:
- Marco Liu: finalize Prometheus recording rules and implement composite_score in staging (ETA 2025-03-10).
- Evelyn Chen: add routing-weight toggle API and a button in dashboard for soft mitigation (ETA 2025-03-17).
- Samir Patel: run 6 week simulation and produce labeled dataset and evaluation spreadsheet (ETA 2025-04-21).
- Priya Desai (owner): consolidate findings and propose Phase 2 alert thresholds after simulation.

Notes to self / rough observations (unpolished):
- Quick look at last 6 incidents: KV miss upticks preceded visible degradation in ~60% cases; allocator backoffs seemed to matter more when workloads had bursty small-shoebox requests.
- Remember: autoscaler is tuned to GPU utilization, not micro-latency; we might need a separate degradation-triggered scale policy.
- Might be worth adding a small ML classifier over 1h windows, but keep first rollout purely rule-based.

Attachments & artifacts to review:
- local notebook: experiments/kv-cache-amplification.ipynb
- sim harness: infra/sim/gpu-noise-hammer (branch: priya/early-warning)
